name: Falafel
description: Crispy, herb-packed chickpea fritters made from dried (never canned) chickpeas

timing.notes: Plus 8-12 hours soaking time for chickpeas and 30-60 min chilling

equipment.notes: For soaking chickpeas - they triple in size
Essential for proper texture - blender won't work
For deep frying - needs to hold 3 inches of oil

equipment.item: Ice cream scoop or falafel scoop

ingredients.notes: MUST use dried chickpeas - canned will not work
Serrano or jalapeño - remove seeds for less heat
Just peel - food processor will chop
Vegetable, canola, or peanut oil. Need 3 inches depth.

prep_steps.instruction: The night before (or 8-12 hours ahead): Place dried chickpeas in a large bowl and cover with several inches of water. They will triple in size.
prep_steps.notes: This step is NON-NEGOTIABLE. Canned chickpeas have too much moisture and will fall apart.

prep_steps.instruction: Set up your staging area: clear counter space near the food processor. Get out 1 small bowl for spices, 1 medium bowl for herb/aromatics, and 1 large bowl for the final mixture. Have your cutting board ready.
prep_steps.notes: The food processor does most of the work, but organized prep makes it smooth

prep_steps.instruction: Drain and rinse the soaked chickpeas thoroughly. Leave in strainer to continue draining.
Roughly chop the onion into large pieces. Add to the medium bowl.
prep_steps.notes: Doesn't need to be precise - food processor will do the work

prep_steps.instruction: Remove stems from parsley, roughly chop leaves. Add to the medium bowl with onion.
Remove stems from cilantro, roughly chop leaves. Add to the medium bowl.
Roughly chop the chile pepper (remove seeds for less heat). Add to the medium bowl.
Peel garlic cloves (leave whole). Add to the medium bowl.
prep_steps.notes: Your medium bowl now has all aromatics: onion, parsley, cilantro, chile, garlic

prep_steps.instruction: Measure all spices into the small bowl: cumin, salt, cardamom, black pepper
Add soaked chickpeas, all aromatics from the medium bowl, and the spice blend to food processor. Pulse until mixture resembles coarse sand - DO NOT over-process to a paste.
prep_steps.notes: The texture should be like coarse sand or bulgur wheat. Over-processing makes gummy falafel.

prep_steps.instruction: Transfer mixture to the large bowl. Add chickpea flour and baking soda. Stir to combine.
Cover bowl and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 1 hour. This firms up the mixture for easier shaping.
prep_steps.notes: Don't skip this - cold mixture holds together better

prep_steps.instruction: Shape falafel into balls or patties using an ice cream scoop, falafel scoop, or your hands. About 2 tablespoons each. Place on a sheet pan or plate.
prep_steps.notes: If mixture is too wet, add 1 tbsp more flour. If too dry, add 1 tsp water or lemon juice.

cook_steps.instruction: Pour oil into heavy-bottomed pot to a depth of 3 inches. Heat over medium heat to 350°F (175°C).

cues.visual: Oil shimmers. A small piece of falafel mixture sizzles immediately when dropped in.

cook_steps.warnings: Use a thermometer - temperature is critical. Too hot = burnt outside, raw inside. Too cool = greasy, falling apart.

cook_steps.instruction: Line a plate with paper towels for draining
Carefully lower 6-8 falafel into the hot oil. Don't overcrowd - they need room to cook evenly.
cook_steps.warnings: Lower gently to avoid splashing hot oil

cook_steps.instruction: Fry until deep golden brown, turning occasionally, 1-2 minutes total

cues.visual: Deep golden brown on all sides, crispy exterior

cook_steps.warnings: Don't let them get too dark - aim for golden, not brown. Internal temp not needed - the outside color is your guide.

cook_steps.instruction: Remove falafel with spider strainer to paper towel-lined plate
Let oil return to 350°F between batches, then repeat with remaining falafel
cook_steps.warnings: Check temperature between batches - it drops when you add cold falafel

finishing.instructions: Serve immediately while hot and crispy. Best with tahini sauce, in pita bread with pickled vegetables, or over a salad.
finishing.make_ahead: The mixture can be made and refrigerated for up to 3 days, or frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw in fridge before shaping. You can also freeze shaped (uncooked) falafel and fry directly from frozen.
finishing.storage: Cooked falafel keep in fridge for 3 days. Reheat in 375°F oven for 10 minutes to re-crisp. They will never be quite as good as fresh.

notes: DRIED chickpeas only - this is non-negotiable. Canned chickpeas are too wet and will disintegrate.
The mixture should look like coarse sand. If you can form a smooth ball, you've over-processed.
If falafel fall apart while frying, the mixture is too wet - add more flour and re-chill.
Can also be baked at 375°F for 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway - but they won't be as crispy.
